steps.message: The Span 2 deck pour has moved to early June, and Vantera is setting the Span 2 deck forms and screed rails the week of May 25, 2026, working from the haunch build-up in the approved girder package. Before the forms go on, check the Span 2 build-up against the contract documents and tell Dana whether it can be used as submitted, and if not, what has to happen before the forms are set and in what order. Dana also wants the memo to carry the Span 2 figures the contract documents give at the profile grade line, with the basis for each: the top-of-girder elevation at the Bent 2 centerline of bearing and the haunch at that bearing, and from those, taking the bearing haunch as the same at both bents, the haunch the forms get built to at midspan and the screed-rail elevation at midspan. The girder package, plans, and the rest of the project record are on the share. One memo for Dana's signature, dated May 21, 2026. Save it as /filesystem/Span2_Haunch_Verification.docx
I'll start by exploring the share to understand what's available.

                                                          SECTION 03300

                              CAST-IN-PLACE STRUCTURAL CONCRETE
 03300.01 — Description
 This Section governs the furnishing of materials, proportioning, mixing, placing, finishing, curing, and acceptance of
 cast-in-place structural concrete for retaining walls, bridge substructure elements (footings, columns, caps,
 wingwalls, and abutment stems), approach slabs, drainage structures, and miscellaneous structural concrete. Work
 shall conform to ACI 318, ACI 301, ACI 305R and ACI 306R as applicable, and AASHTO LRFD Bridge
 Construction Specifications, except where superseded by the requirements below.

 03300.02 — Mix Classes and Specified Strength
 Concrete shall be furnished in the mix classes tabulated below. The 28-day compressive strength (f′c) shown is the
 specified strength for acceptance under 03300.06.

             Class       Application                                                                    Specified 28-day f′c

                A        Bridge substructure — footings, columns, caps, abutment stems                         4,500 psi

                B        Retaining-wall stems and footings (Reaches R-1, R-2, R-3)                             4,000 psi

                C        Drainage structures, headwalls, junction boxes                                        3,500 psi

                D        Bridge deck (composite with prestressed girders)                                      4,500 psi

                E        Concrete pavement (see Section 401)                                               Per Section 401

                F        Sidewalks, driveways, non-structural flatwork                                         3,000 psi

 The retaining-wall mix (Class B) shall be proportioned to a specified 28-day compressive strength of 4,000 psi,
 with a maximum water-cementitious materials ratio of 0.45, minimum cement content of 611 lb/CY, entrained air
 5.5% ± 1.5%, and slump 4 in. ± 1 in. at the point of placement. Cementitious materials shall consist of Type I/II
 portland cement with a Class F fly ash replacement of not less than 20% and not more than 30% by mass of total
 cementitious materials.

 03300.03 — Submittals
 Mix designs shall be submitted to the Engineer for each class not less than 30 calendar days prior to first placement.
 Each mix design shall include:
         (a) Trial batch data with 28-day cylinder breaks demonstrating a strength margin (f′cr) computed per ACI 301
         §4.2.3;
         (b) Certified aggregate gradations, specific gravities, and absorption;
         (c) Admixture certifications (Type A, D, F, or G per ASTM C494);
         (d) Statement of proposed batch plant, transit time to site, and placement rate;
         (e) Curing plan.
 No placement shall proceed against an unapproved mix design.

 03300.04 — Batching, Delivery, and Placement


Technical Specifications — Book 2 of 2 • FINAL — Issued for Bid • October 15, 2024                                                    Page 3
 Larkspur Civil Group, Inc.                                                  Wren Parkway Widening & Pecan Creek Bridge Replacement — WP-2401



 Batching shall conform to ASTM C94. Time from introduction of mixing water to completion of discharge shall not
 exceed 90 minutes (60 minutes when ambient temperature exceeds 85 °F). Water added at the site to restore slump
 shall not cause the water-cementitious ratio to exceed the mix design value; retempering with water is prohibited.
 Placement in lifts shall not exceed 12 ft in vertical rise. Consolidation shall be by internal vibration; the Contractor
 shall have redundant vibrators on-site during placement. Cold-weather placement (ambient < 40 °F or falling to < 40
 °F within 24 hours) shall follow ACI 306R; hot-weather placement (ambient > 90 °F or forecast to exceed 90 °F
 within 24 hours) shall follow ACI 305R.

 03300.05 — Curing
 All structural concrete shall be moist-cured or membrane-cured for a minimum of 7 calendar days. Water curing is
 required for bridge decks and for any Class A element with an exposed face wider than 3 ft. Curing compounds shall
 be Type 2 (white pigmented) conforming to ASTM C309.

 03300.06 — Acceptance and Strength Evaluation
 03300.06.A — Sampling
 Concrete shall be sampled per ASTM C172 at the point of discharge into the forms. Frequency of sampling for
 acceptance shall be:
         (a) One set (four cylinders) per 50 CY placed, but not less than one set per placement per class per day;
         (b) Two cylinders shall be tested at 28 days for acceptance; one at 7 days for information; one held as a
         laboratory reserve.
 Cylinders shall be cast, cured, transported, and tested per ASTM C31 and ASTM C39 by the Owner's independent
 materials testing laboratory (Pinnacle Testing Services LLC). The average of the two 28-day cylinders from one
 sample constitutes a strength test for purposes of this Section.

 03300.06.B — Acceptance Criteria for Strength
 The strength of each class of concrete shall be considered satisfactory when both of the following are met:
         (a) No individual 28-day strength test result falls more than 500 psi below the specified compressive strength
         f′c. For the Class B retaining-wall mix specified at 4,000 psi, this means no individual strength test result
         shall fall below 3,500 psi.
         (b) The average of any three consecutive strength tests equals or exceeds the specified compressive strength
         f′c.
 Failure to satisfy criterion (a) — that is, the occurrence of any individual test result more than 500 psi below the
 specified strength — shall be cause for the Engineer to require an investigation of the strength of the concrete in
 place, in accordance with ACI 318 §26.12 and 03300.06.C below. Failure to satisfy criterion (b) shall require the
 Contractor to take steps to raise the average strength of subsequent production.

 03300.06.C — Investigation of Low-Strength Test Results — Core Sampling
 When an individual strength test falls more than 500 psi below the specified strength, or when there is other cause to
 doubt the strength of concrete in place, the Engineer may direct that the strength of the concrete in place be evaluated
 by drilled cores taken and tested per ASTM C42. Cores shall be drilled from the questioned placement not sooner
 than 14 calendar days after placement (measured from placement date to core-drilling date) and not later than 45
 calendar days after placement, unless otherwise directed by the Engineer.
 Three cores shall be taken from the area represented by the failing strength test. The location and orientation of cores
 shall be selected by the Engineer to represent the questioned concrete without compromising the structural integrity

Technical Specifications — Book 2 of 2 • FINAL — Issued for Bid • October 15, 2024                                                    Page 4
 Larkspur Civil Group, Inc.                                                  Wren Parkway Widening & Pecan Creek Bridge Replacement — WP-2401



 of the element. Core holes shall be filled with a non-shrink structural grout of strength not less than the specified
 strength f′c.
 The concrete in the area represented by a set of three cores shall be considered structurally adequate — and the
 placement shall be accepted in place — when both of the following are satisfied:
         (a) The average compressive strength of the three cores equals or exceeds 85% of the specified strength
         (0.85 × f′c). For the Class B retaining-wall mix specified at 4,000 psi, this threshold is 3,400 psi.
         (b) No individual core has a compressive strength less than 75% of the specified strength (0.75 × f′c). For the
         Class B retaining-wall mix specified at 4,000 psi, this threshold is 3,000 psi.
 Core results shall be corrected for length-to-diameter ratio per ASTM C42 §7.7 before comparison to these criteria.
 Cores that do not satisfy both criteria shall be cause for the Engineer to require load testing, structural analysis
 reduction, replacement of the concrete, or such other remedial measures as the Engineer determines are required to
 establish the structural adequacy of the element.

 03300.06.D — Payment During Investigation
 No payment shall be made for concrete under investigation until the investigation is concluded and the Engineer has
 issued a written disposition. When cores establish that the placement is acceptable in place under 03300.06.C, no
 reduction in payment shall be taken solely on account of low cylinder breaks; the placement shall be paid as bid.
 Nothing in 03300.06 relieves the Contractor of the obligation to furnish concrete meeting the specified strength at the
 point of delivery. Repeated occurrences of individual test failures against criterion (a) shall be cause for the Engineer
 to direct that the mix design be re-proportioned and re-submitted before further placement.

 03300.07 — Tolerances
 Formed surface tolerances shall meet ACI 117 Class B for concealed backfilled surfaces and Class A for
 architecturally exposed surfaces. Vertical alignment tolerance for retaining-wall stems shall not exceed 1 in. in 10 ft,
 and not more than 2 in. cumulative over any single stem lift.

 03300.08 — Method of Measurement and Payment
 Cast-in-place structural concrete shall be measured by the cubic yard, computed from plan dimensions, of each class
 in place and accepted. Payment shall be at the contract unit price per cubic yard for the class furnished and includes
 all forming, reinforcement placement supervision, batching, mixing, transporting, placing, consolidating, finishing,
 curing, cylinder casting cooperation, and appurtenant work. Reinforcement is paid separately under Section 03200.

                                                            SECTION 401

                             PORTLAND CEMENT CONCRETE PAVEMENT
 401.01 — Description
 This Section governs construction of jointed plain concrete pavement (JPCP) for the widened travel lanes of Wren
 Parkway between Stations 100+00 and 226+00, including the bridge-approach transition slabs. Work shall conform
 to AASHTO M 148, AASHTO M 249, ACI 325.12R, and the standard details in Sheets D-1 through D-6 of the
 Contract Drawings.

 401.02 — Materials
 Cement: Type I/II portland cement conforming to ASTM C150. Blended cements per ASTM C595 (Type IL) may
 be substituted with the Engineer's written approval.
 Coarse Aggregate: Crushed limestone conforming to ASTM C33 Size No. 57 or No. 67. Los Angeles abrasion loss
 (ASTM C131) shall not exceed 40%. Micro-Deval loss (ASTM D6928) shall not exceed 18%.
 Fine Aggregate: Natural sand conforming to ASTM C33 with fineness modulus between 2.6 and 3.0.
 Admixtures: Air-entraining admixture per ASTM C260. Water-reducing admixtures per ASTM C494 Types A, D,
 or F.
 Reinforcement: Deformed epoxy-coated dowel bars per ASTM A615 Grade 60 with ASTM A934 coating, 1-1/2
 in. diameter × 18 in. long at transverse contraction joints; smooth tie bars No. 5 × 30 in. at longitudinal joints.

 401.03 — Mix Design
 Pavement concrete shall be proportioned for a specified 28-day flexural strength of 650 psi (third-point loading,
 ASTM C78), corresponding to an approximate specified compressive strength of 4,500 psi. Maximum
 water-cementitious ratio shall be 0.42. Air content 6.0% ± 1.5%. Slump 1.5 in. ± 1.0 in. for slipform placement, 3.0
 in. ± 1.0 in. for fixed-form placement.

 401.04 — Placement
 Pavement shall be placed in lanes not less than one lane-width wide. Slipform paving is preferred; fixed-form
 placement is permitted at bridge-approach transitions and irregular geometry. Placement shall not occur when
 ambient temperature is below 40 °F or above 90 °F, unless the Contractor submits and the Engineer approves a hot-
 or cold-weather placement plan.
 Transverse contraction joints shall be sawn at 15 ft centers to a depth of one-third the slab thickness. Sawing shall
 commence as soon as the concrete can be cut without raveling and shall be complete before random cracking
 initiates, typically within 4 to 12 hours after placement depending on weather.

 401.05 — Curing
 A white-pigmented curing compound conforming to ASTM C309 Type 2 shall be applied at the manufacturer's
 minimum coverage rate immediately after final finishing.

 401.06 — Acceptance
 Pavement is accepted on the basis of thickness (measured from cores per AASHTO T 148), flexural strength (beams
 per ASTM C78), and profile smoothness (International Roughness Index, IRI, measured per ASTM E1926 on all

                                                            SECTION 502

                                    PRESTRESSED CONCRETE GIRDERS
 502.01 — Description
 This Section governs the fabrication, handling, storage, transport, erection, and post-tensioning (where applicable) of
 prestressed concrete girders for the three-span, 285-ft Pecan Creek bridge replacement. Girders shall be Type
 AASHTO Bulb-Tee BT-72 or equivalent, continuous for live load at the interior bents, as shown on Structural Sheets
 S-5 through S-9.

 502.02 — Materials
 Concrete: Specified 28-day compressive strength f′c = 8,500 psi; specified strength at release f′ci = 6,000 psi.
 Materials shall conform to Section 03300 except where superseded here. Maximum water-cementitious ratio 0.38.
 Prestressing Strand: Low-relaxation seven-wire strand, 0.6-in. nominal diameter, conforming to ASTM A416
 Grade 270.
 Mild Reinforcement: ASTM A615 Grade 60 or ASTM A706 Grade 60, epoxy-coated in the deck-embedment
 zone.

 502.03 — Fabrication
 Fabrication shall be performed only in a plant certified under the Precast/Prestressed Concrete Institute (PCI) Plant
 Certification Program in categories B4 (bridge products) and pre-approved by the Engineer. Working shop drawings
 shall be submitted to the Engineer per the requirements of Section 01330 and shall bear the seal of a Texas licensed
 Professional Engineer.
 Detensioning shall not occur until cylinders cast alongside the girders demonstrate a compressive strength equal to or
 greater than the release strength specified above. Cylinders shall be match-cured to the girder ambient.

 502.04 — Handling, Storage, and Transport
 Girders shall be handled at the lift points shown on the shop drawings only. Girders shall be stored upright on
 supports at the specified bearing locations, not more than 6 in. inboard of the girder ends, with adequate
 cross-bracing to prevent lateral rotation.

 502.05 — Erection
 Erection shall follow a sealed erection plan submitted by the Contractor and approved by the Engineer prior to first
 pick. The plan shall address crane picks, lateral stability at set, temporary bracing until the diaphragms are placed,
 and the sequence of diaphragm placement.

 502.06 — Deck Continuity
 Continuity for live load at the interior bents shall be developed by cast-in-place deck reinforcement over the bent
 caps as detailed on Sheet S-7. Deck placement sequence shall be:
         (1) Positive-moment regions of Spans 1 and 3 first;
         (2) Positive-moment region of Span 2 second;
         (3) Negative-moment regions over Bent 1 and Bent 2 last.

 QUESTION 1 — CONTINUOUS DECK POUR, PECAN CREEK BRIDGE
 Reference Documents:
  • Plan Sheet B-11 — Deck Pour Sequence and Construction Joints (Rev 0, 10/15/2024, sealed Priya Raman, PE #121408)
  • Plan Sheet B-07 — Girder Layout and Framing Plan (Rev 0, 10/15/2024)
  • Plan Sheet B-10 — Deck Reinforcement Plan (Rev 0, 10/15/2024)
  • Baseline schedule, Update 15 (data date 04/30/2026) — bridge substructure critical path
 Background.
 Sheet B-11 prescribes a four-pour sequence for the 285-ft, three-span (90 + 105 + 90) prestressed concrete girder deck as follows:
   1. Pour 1 — Positive-moment region of Span 1, from centerline bearing at Abutment 1 to a construction joint located 0.15 L■ into Span
      2 measured from Bent 1.
   2. Pour 2 — Positive-moment region of Span 3, from centerline bearing at Abutment 2 to a construction joint located 0.15 L■ into Span
      2 measured from Bent 2; Pour 2 not placed until Pour 1 attains 70% f′c.
   3. Pour 3 — Positive-moment region of Span 2, between the two construction joints; not placed until Pours 1 and 2 have attained 70%
      f′c.
   4. Pour 4 — Negative-moment regions over Bents 1 and 2, placed last as two closure pours after Pours 1, 2, and 3 have attained f′c.
 Sheet B-11, General Note 3, states that continuous single pours across the entire deck are prohibited by that sheet and that any deviation
 from the sequence above requires a sealed engineering analysis submitted and approved prior to placement.

 Vantera proposes to place the remaining deck - the Span 2 positive-moment region (Pour 3) together with the negative-moment closure
 pours over Bents 1 and 2 (Pour 4) - as a single continuous pour in lieu of the sequenced Pours 3 and 4 on Sheet B-11. Pours 1 and 2 (the
 positive-moment regions of Spans 1 and 3) are excluded. Vantera's rationale:

   • The 70% f′c wait between Pours 1, 2, and 3, plus the additional f′c wait before the closure Pour 4, imposes approximately five calendar
     days of pour-to-pour cure delay on the critical path as currently sequenced. A single continuous placement eliminates those inter-pour
     waits.
   • Bridge-substructure critical path currently shows zero float in Update 15 (11/20/2026 forecast). The recovery of five calendar days is a
     direct schedule buy-back for Substantial Completion.
   • Vantera has provided single-pour continuous deck placements on prior projects of comparable length and would furnish the placement
     plan (pump layout, mix design with retarder, finishing crew rotation, and cold-joint contingency) as a separate submittal if approved in
     principle.
   • The retarded mix and continuous placement would, in Vantera's view, permit hydration to advance concurrently across positive- and
     negative-moment regions rather than sequentially, and thereby avoid the reflected cold-joint at the interior construction joints called
     out on B-11.
 Requested Action from the Engineer.
 Vantera requests the Engineer's approval to place the deck as a continuous deck pour in a single monolithic placement in lieu of the Sheet
 B-11 four-pour sequence, or, in the alternative, the Engineer's written direction identifying the specific sealed engineering analysis and
 submittal content that must be provided for the proposed continuous placement to be considered under Sheet B-11 General Note 3.
 Schedule Consequence.
 Response is required by 06/03/2026 in order to preserve the early-June deck placement window and the five-day schedule recovery on the
 bridge-substructure critical path. A denial response, or a response requiring a further sealed analysis submittal, will cause Vantera to revert
 to the Sheet B-11 four-pour sequence, with no schedule recovery available from this RFI.

 QUESTION 3 — GUARDRAIL HEIGHT AT BRIDGE APPROACHES
 Reference Documents:
  • Specification Section 606 — Guardrail (Issued for Bid 10/15/2024)
  • Plan Sheet R-11 — Guardrail Details at Bridge Approaches (Rev 0, 10/15/2024)

 Background.
 The contract documents contain two different top-of-rail height requirements for the guardrail at the Pecan Creek bridge approaches (Sta.
 167+00 to Sta. 167+90 west approach; Sta. 169+85 to Sta. 170+75 east approach):
   • Specification Section 606.03.B — Bridge Approaches. States that the approach guardrail shall be 31-inch MGS (Midwest Guardrail
      System), MASH TL-3 eligible, with the top of rail set at a nominal 31 in. above the adjacent finished shoulder grade, with a stiffness

      606 is marked FINAL and dated 10/15/2024 in the Issued for Bid stamp on the specification cover.
   • Sheet R-11, Note 1, and City Engineer Directive Memo dated 01/15/2025. Sheet R-11 shows the approach guardrail at a 36-inch
      top-of-rail height (modified-height MGS on W6×8.5 posts at 6′-3″ spacing, 12-gauge W-beam), and includes a standing note citing the
      01/15/2025 memo as the governing authority; the memo, signed by Sam DeLuca, PE (City Engineer), directs 36-inch top-of-rail at the
      bridge approaches with the engineering basis stated as preservation of a 33-inch effective height after the 3-inch programmed HMAC
      overlay.
   • Submittal 606-02, Rev 1 was returned “Approved as Noted @ 36-inch per 01/15/2025 memo” on 03/03/2025.
 Vantera has raised this conflict previously (see prior RFI-043, closed 04/27/2026, and Submittal 606-02, Rev 1) and continues to view
 the FINAL Specification Section 606 language as the governing crashworthy-height requirement, with the 31-inch MGS system being the
 FHWA-eligibility-tested configuration. Vantera notes that the 3-inch programmed overlay premise on which the 01/15/2025 memo relies is
 a future-work assumption that is not part of Vantera's current scope of pay quantities, and that Sheet R-11 Note 2 acknowledges that “In the
 event of any conflict between this Sheet R-11 and Specification Section 606 as to guardrail height at bridge approaches, this sheet governs,”

 Vantera has installed approach guardrail material sufficient for 31-inch installation and has priced the balance of the work at the 31-inch
 configuration in its unit-price bid. The 36-inch approach-rail quantities were carried into CO-07 (04/14/2026) without Vantera's concession

 Requested Action from the Engineer.
 Vantera requests final written direction from the Engineer on the governing top-of-rail height at the Pecan Creek bridge approaches,
 addressing specifically:
  1. Whether the governing height is 36-inch (per Sheet R-11 Note 1 and the 01/15/2025 City Engineer Directive Memo) or 31-inch (per

  2. The document-hierarchy basis on which the Engineer determines the governing requirement, including how the “FINAL”-labeled
      Specification Section 606 is reconciled with the later-dated 01/15/2025 memo, and
  3. Whether Sheet R-11 Note 2 — asserting that Sheet R-11 governs over Section 606 at the bridge approaches — is the Engineer's
      controlling direction.
 Schedule Consequence.

1.2 Encountered Condition
Beginning with the first Bent 2 shaft on 03/17/2026 and continuing through the shafts advanced 03/18/2026 – 03/31/2026, Vantera's drill crew has

 • Recovery of angular limestone fragments in the auger flights above the design top-of-rock elevation, in intervals where soft residuum or weathered
    material was anticipated by the crew.
 • Instances of short intervals of relatively hard drilling followed by softer or seam-like intervals below, with return to hard drilling again below the
   seam, before entry into what the crew has described as continuous sound rock at depth.
 • Extended tool changes and torque adjustments compared with the durations assumed in Vantera's approved production plan for the
   residuum-through-rock transition at Bent 2.
The 03/17/2026 daily report (Larkspur DR-0071) records the first of these observations. Vantera has continued to advance the shafts in accordance with

2.1 Response to Item 1 — Top-of-Rock Elevation Applicable to Bent 2
                                     tion applicable to the Bent 2 shafts, as established in the Contract Documents,
                                     in the




The Contract Documents incorporate, by reference, the Redoak Geotechnical Investigation Report of 08/22/2024, including its Appendix A boring logs
(B-1 through B-12) and the descriptive sections of the report body. Boring B-7 is bound in the Appendix A boring log package in the ordinary numerical
sequence B-1 through B-12 and is not distinguished in that pagination from the other bridge-substructure borings (B-1 at Abut. 1, B-6 at Bent 1, and B-8
at Abut. 2).
2.2 Response to Item 2 — Datum
The elevation of 512.3 ft reported at Boring B-7, and every elevation cited in this response, is stated on the project vertical datum, NAVD 88. The
project vertical datum is NAVD 88, as established by the survey control memorandum prepared by Beau Terlingua, RPLS #6612, dated 05/09/2024, and
as identified on the sealed Contract Drawings. All boring log elevations in Appendix A of the Redoak Geotechnical Investigation Report are stated on
NAVD 88. The Contractor is reminded that any legacy record referenced during construction that is not on the project datum must be converted to
NAVD 88 before it is used in any elevation-critical comparison.
2.3 Response to Item 3 — Variability Disclosed in the Report
The Contract Documents also disclose that the top-of-rock surface across this corridor is variable. Section §5.2 of the sealed Redoak Geotechnical
Investigation Report (“Pinnacled-Limestone Variability”) states, in operative part:
         “…top-of-rock may fluctuate ±6 ft over ~30-ft lateral offsets due to karst weathering; localized rises and pinnacles common. Contractor
         should anticipate variable drilling behavior.”
Section §5.2 further advises the Contractor, in the subsections immediately following the quoted sentence, that (a) the actual top of rock at each
production shaft may differ from the log at the nearest boring by an amount within the range noted above; (b) pinnacled top of rock and karst features —
including clay-seam runs and localized voids — are inherent to the Edwards Group at this site, and variable drilling behavior (rapid transitions from soft
residuum into hard limestone, sudden loss of auger torque across seams, and short “false-refusal” pinnacles above the sound-rock horizon) should be
anticipated; and (c) field verification of sound-rock elevation at each production shaft is required, and equipment capable of handling both
hard-limestone drilling and soft-seam clean-out within the same shaft without extended re-mobilization should be provided.
Bent 2 lies within the corridor of §5.2 applicability. The nearest borings to Bent 2 are B-6 (Bent 1, Sta. 167+90; top of rock 510.7 ft NAVD 88)
approximately 105 ft west, and B-8 (Abut. 2, Sta. 169+85; top of rock 511.9 ft NAVD 88) approximately 90 ft east. The top-of-rock elevations logged at
B-6, B-7, and B-8 are internally consistent with the ±6 ft over ~30-ft-offset variability disclosed in §5.2.
The field behavior described in Part 1, §1.2 above — a rapid drop in penetration rate at elevations near or above 512.3 ft NAVD 88, recovery of angular
limestone fragments in the auger above sound-rock elevation, short intervals of harder drilling above softer or seam-like intervals with a return to hard
drilling below, and variability of tool response within a single shaft — is the behavior expressly anticipated in §5.2 of the sealed report as the character
of the karstic top-of-rock surface at this site. It is consistent with, and disclosed by, the Contract Documents.
Redoak Geoscience LLC, as sealing engineer of the Geotechnical Investigation Report, has re-reviewed the Boring B-7 record (signed and sealed
boring log, field driller's log, photographic record of core runs, retained rock cores in the Redoak Austin core library, and laboratory UCS reports) and
has issued a signed and sealed Geotechnical Addendum Letter dated April 21, 2026 (Redoak Addendum LTR-RG-2026-018), re-confirming top of
sound limestone at Boring B-7 at 512.3 ft NAVD 88 and confirming that the encountered condition at Bent 2 is consistent with the sealed geotechnical
record. A copy of that addendum letter is enclosed for the Contractor's file.

2.4 Response to Item 4 — Direction on Continued Production
Vantera is directed to continue Bent 2 shaft installation in accordance with the approved Drilled Shaft Installation Plan (Submittal 421-01) and Contract
Specification Section 455. Field verification of sound-rock elevation at each production shaft is required per §5.2 of the sealed geotechnical report and
per Specification Section 455.6. The Larkspur field inspector (Tom Herrera, EIT) will continue to observe and document the sound-rock verification at
each shaft in the daily reports.
Continuation of production at Bent 2 pursuant to this direction does not, by itself, constitute a waiver by the Contractor of any right the Contractor may
separately assert under the Contract.
2.5 Determination
Based on Sections 2.1 through 2.4 above, and on the Redoak Geotechnical Addendum Letter dated April 21, 2026:

 • The variability of the top-of-rock surface, and the variable drilling behavior described in Part 1, are expressly disclosed in §5.2 of the sealed

 This memorandum establishes the horizontal and vertical control framework for WP-2401 and directs all design, construction, and

 WP-2401 shall reference the datums identified below.

 The primary vertical control point for WP-2401 has been recovered, verified by differential leveling from published NGS control, and adopted
 as follows:
Benchmark        Description                                               Station / Location                                       Published Elevation
   BM-01         Top of nut, TxDOT ROW monument                            Sta. 105+00, Wren Parkway centerline                       517.62 ft NAVD 88

 referenced to BM-01 by second-order Class II differential leveling; see accompanying control point tabulation issued under the survey
 deliverable.
 4. LEGACY DATUM CONVERSION
 Portions of the record background — including the 1998 utility as-built plans, prior floodplain studies, and certain adjoining plat sheets —
 were prepared on NGVD 29. To prevent inconsistencies between record data and current project elevations, the following rule shall apply
 project-wide:
        Legacy NGVD 29 elevations must be converted to NAVD 88 by adding 0.83 ft prior to comparison against project
        elevations.
 The +0.83 ft shift was determined by direct leveling ties between BM-01 (NAVD 88) and two NGVD 29 monuments referenced on the 1998
 utility as-builts, and cross-checked against the NGS VERTCON model for this corridor. The offset is uniform across the project limits for the
 precision required by this work.
 Designers, inspectors, and subconsultants shall not compare, plot, or reconcile any elevation obtained from an NGVD 29 source against a
 project (NAVD 88) elevation without first applying the +0.83 ft conversion. Any drawing, log, or report that carries a datum other than NAVD
 88 shall so state on its face; converted values shall be annotated "converted from NGVD 29, +0.83 ft."

approximately 0.42% grade, discharging through headwall HW-1 into Pecan Creek approximately 45 ft downstream of the west abutment. Pipe class

contained in the Storm Drainage Report for Project WP-2401 dated 10/15/2024, Section 4 (Trunk Line B-2), as follows:

     • Design flow: Q25 = C · i · A ≈ 57.9 cfs.
     • Manning capacity of 24-inch RCP at n = 0.013, S = 0.0042, flowing full ≈ 14.7 cfs — insufficient to convey Q25 = 57.9 cfs; run would

     recomputed 25-year HGL remains at least 0.5 ft below the lowest adjacent inlet throat, meeting the Storm Drainage Report Section 4.1 criterion.

        Abut. 2 (east)                     B-8                    511.9 ft                          503.9 ft                       8.0 ft

The 8-foot rock-socket length shown is a minimum. The design shaft-tip elevation is the design value at each location; the actual required tip is a
function of the top of rock actually encountered at each shaft.
Clarification 2.2 — Rock-socket length as measured in the field. The required 8-foot minimum rock socket shall be measured from the actual top of
sound Class II or better limestone encountered at each shaft — not from the design top-of-rock elevation shown on Sheet B-16 or on Sheet B-04 (Bent
2 Details). Where the top of rock is encountered above the design elevation, the shaft tip may be adjusted upward provided the 8-foot minimum
rock-socket length in sound limestone is preserved. Where the top of rock is encountered below the design elevation, the shaft tip shall be adjusted
downward such that the 8-foot minimum rock-socket length in sound limestone is preserved.
Consistent with Sheet B-17, Note 6, if the actual top of rock encountered differs from the design elevation shown on Sheet B-16 by more than 3 feet in
either direction, the Contractor shall stop and notify the Engineer prior to placement of concrete. The Engineer will determine, in writing, the required
shaft-tip elevation for the affected shaft.
Bidders are advised that the sealed Geotechnical Report by Redoak Geoscience LLC (Section 5.2) notes that pinnacled-limestone lateral variability
may reach ±6 feet over lateral offsets of approximately 30 feet, owing to karst weathering, and the design accommodates such variability by anchoring
the rock-socket requirement to the rock actually encountered.
Clarification 2.3 — Measurement and payment. Payment for Bid Item 421 shall be made at the Contract unit price per linear foot of completed drilled
shaft, measured from the design shaft-tip elevation to the top of shaft as shown on the Plans (i.e., the bottom of column at each Bent, and the bottom of
footing/pedestal at each Abutment). Where the shaft is extended below the design tip in accordance with Clarification 2.2, the added length shall be
paid at the Contract unit price per linear foot of Bid Item 421 up to a maximum added length of two (2) feet per shaft; added length in excess of two
(2) feet per shaft shall be compensated by Change Order pursuant to Contract §11 (Changes in the Work). Where the shaft is shortened above the
design tip in accordance with Clarification 2.2 (i.e., because rock was encountered higher than shown), the paid length shall be reduced by the actual
amount by which the shaft is shortened.
Clarification 2.4 — Temporary casing. Temporary casing to the top of rock, where the Contractor elects or is required to use casing for hole stability,
is considered subsidiary to Bid Item 421 and shall not be a separately paid item. Casing shall be advanced and removed in accordance with Sheet
B-17, Note 3, maintaining a minimum concrete head to prevent bond loss. Permanent casing in the rock socket is not required and shall not be
installed unless directed in writing by the Engineer.




Addendum No. 1 — Project WP-2401 — dated November 7, 2024                                                                                     Page 3 of 5
 Clarification 2.5 — Rock coring at Engineer's direction. Where the Engineer directs rock coring at a shaft location to verify soundness of the
limestone at socket depth, the coring shall be performed by the Contractor and reimbursed under Bid Item 421-A — Rock Coring at Drilled Shafts,
unit price per linear foot of core recovered. Bidders shall unit-price Bid Item 421-A on the Bid Form. The Bid Form estimated quantity for Bid Item
421-A is one hundred twenty (120) linear feet, an estimate for bidding purposes only; final quantity shall be that actually directed and performed.
Clarification 2.6 — Non-destructive testing (sonic integrity, crosshole sonic logging). Consistent with Sheet B-17, Note 7, the Engineer may direct
sonic-integrity testing (SIT) or crosshole sonic logging (CSL) at any shaft as a condition of acceptance. When the Engineer directs such testing, it shall
be performed by an independent testing firm retained and paid directly by the Owner; the Contractor shall provide reasonable access, cure time, and
coordination for the testing at no additional cost. Provisions for CSL access tubes, where CSL is elected in advance of concrete placement, shall be as
directed by the Engineer and are subsidiary to Bid Item 421.
Clarification 2.7 — Inspection and drill-cutting logs. In accordance with Sheet B-17, Note 5, the Engineer or the Engineer's designated inspector shall
witness placement of every shaft. The Contractor shall log drill cuttings continuously and shall submit the log to the Engineer within twenty-four (24)
hours of completion of each shaft. Concrete placement shall be by tremie or free-fall not exceeding 5 feet; slump 7″–9″ for tremie placement.
Clarification 2.8 — No change to design elevations at Bent 2. For avoidance of doubt, the design top of rock at Bent 2 is 512.3 ft NAVD 88 (per
Boring B-7) and the design shaft tip at Bent 2 is 504.3 ft NAVD 88 (yielding 8.0 ft embedment below top of rock and 8.0 ft embedment below the
rock-controlled scour floor). These values are unchanged by this Addendum.

A one-dimensional steady-flow model of Pecan Creek from approximately 800 ft upstream of the west
    abutment to 600 ft downstream of the east abutment was developed in HEC-RAS v6.4.1 (USACE HEC). Cross
    sections were cut from the 2023 topographic survey provided by Larkspur survey staff (surveyor of record Beau
    Terlingua, RPLS #6612), supplemented by field cross-section checks performed on 06/07/2024. Manning's
    roughness values were assigned:
      • n = 0.035 in the main channel (limestone with gravel/cobble in pool zones, some low vegetation on point
         bars);
      • n = 0.065 to 0.080 in the vegetated overbanks (dense grass with intermittent brush and mid-story trees).
    The proposed bridge was modeled at its final geometry: three spans (90 ft, 105 ft, 90 ft), low-chord elevation
    528.6 ft NAVD 88 at midspan, and semi-circular-nose piers on 48-inch drilled shafts. Bridge scour options in
    HEC-RAS were used for reporting; scour computations were performed by hand and by spreadsheet in

6. HYDROLOGIC AND HYDRAULIC BASIS

7. FREEBOARD AND LOW-CHORD REQUIREMENT
Bridge low chord shall be set not less than 524.4 ft NAVD 88 at the controlling section, providing a minimum of 2.0 ft of freeboard above
the 100-year water-surface elevation of 522.4 ft NAVD 88 in accordance with Chapter 34, § 34-118(c)(2) of the City Code. Any
subsequent revision to the low-chord elevation shown on the approved plans shall require written amendment of this permit prior to
construction.
8. SCOUR PROTECTION
Scour countermeasures shall conform to the Larkspur Scour Evaluation (FHWA HEC-18 / HEC-23 methodology). Rock riprap placed at
abutments and bank-protection reaches shall have a nominal median stone size of D50 = 18 in per HEC-23 Design Guideline 11 (abutment
riprap sizing). Riprap gradation, filter, and thickness shall conform to the Contract Documents (Sheet S-3R, IFC set). Bent 2 drilled-shaft
tip elevation of 504.3 ft NAVD 88 provides 8 ft of embedment below the rock-controlled scour floor at 512.3 ft NAVD 88 and satisfies
FHWA scour-protection requirements at rock-founded substructure units.
9. CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL
This permit is issued subject to the following conditions. Failure to comply is grounds for revocation and enforcement under Chapter 34.
1.     Construction shall conform to the plans and specifications identified in Section 10 below. No deviation affecting the hydraulic
       opening, low-chord elevation, or floodway boundary is permitted without written amendment.
2.     In-stream construction activities shall be limited to the period from October 1 through May 31 to the extent practicable, and shall not
       be undertaken when the National Weather Service forecast probability of measurable precipitation within 48 hours exceeds 40
       percent.
3.     Temporary causeways, cofferdams, or diversions shall be sized to convey the 2-year storm without loss of freeboard on upstream
       properties and shall be removed in full at completion, restoring the pre-construction channel section.
4.     Riprap of D50 = 18 in shall be placed at abutments and at bank-protection reaches as detailed on Sheet S-3R prior to seasonal
       high-flow events and prior to removal of temporary works.
5.     The Permittee shall maintain the SWPPP in accordance with TCEQ TXR150000 and the project ESC Plan. A copy shall be kept at the
       field office and available on request.
6.     Following completion, the Permittee shall submit a signed and sealed as-built low-chord elevation certification for the controlling
       section, together with an as-built cross-section of the completed channel and riprap.
7.     Any encountered condition materially different from the H&H model assumptions — including but not limited to channel migration,
       bank sloughing, or blockage of hydraulic opening — shall be reported to the Floodplain Administrator within five (5) business days.
8.     This permit does not relieve the Permittee of the obligation to obtain any other required federal, state, or local authorization, including
       USACE Section 404, TCEQ Section 401 water-quality certification, and TPWD coordination as applicable.

PRE-BID MEETING MINUTES


1. ATTENDANCE
Owner — City of Milbrook
Engineer — Larkspur Civil Group, Inc.
Prospective Bidders
A sign-in sheet was circulated and is retained in the project bid file. Attendance at this pre-bid conference was non-mandatory; failure of a prospective bidder to attend does not disqualify a bid.
2. CALL TO ORDER
Marcus Okafor (Larkspur) opened the meeting at 10:00 a.m., introduced the project team, and stated the purpose of the conference: to walk prospective bidders through the scope, contract framework, and bidding schedule, and to receive written or verbal questions that will be addressed either in these minutes or by formal addendum. Mr. Okafor confirmed that the project was advertised on October 28, 2024, and that Bid Documents (Advertisement, Instructions to Bidders, Bid Form, Contract, General & Special Conditions, Technical Specifications dated October 15, 2024, and the Plans dated for bidding) are available through the City's procurement portal.
Sam DeLuca (City Engineer) welcomed the bidders on behalf of the City of Milbrook and reiterated the City's commitment to a competitive, transparent bid process and to on-schedule delivery of the corridor improvement.
3. PROJECT OVERVIEW
Marcus Okafor presented the project scope, summarized as follows:
3.1 Corridor Widening.  Widening of Wren Parkway from an existing 2-lane rural section to a 4-lane divided urban section with 8-ft shoulders and 6-ft sidewalks, extending 2.4 miles (approximately 12,600 linear feet) between the west limit at Old Millican Road (Sta. 100+00) and the east limit at McKinney Boulevard (Sta. 226+00).
3.2 Pecan Creek Bridge Replacement.  Complete removal of the existing 1962 two-span steel-girder bridge over Pecan Creek and construction of a new 285-ft three-span prestressed concrete girder bridge (spans of 90 ft — 105 ft — 90 ft), continuous for live load, founded on 48-inch drilled shafts socketed a minimum of 8 ft into sound limestone at 40 ksf allowable end bearing. Abutment 1 (west) is at Sta. 167+00 and Abutment 2 (east) at Sta. 169+85; interior bents are at Sta. 167+90 (Bent 1) and Sta. 168+95 (Bent 2). Twelve drilled shafts total.
3.3 Ancillary Work.  Storm-drainage trunk system (12 runs) sized to a 25-year design storm using the Rational Method; MSE and reinforced-concrete retaining walls; pavement structure per the Typical Sections; signing, striping, and pavement markings; traffic-signal modification at the McKinney Boulevard intersection; illumination; MGS guardrail per Spec Section 606; and full erosion/sediment control under an approved SWPPP.
3.4 Scope Coordination Notes.
The corridor is under existing traffic; a Traffic Control Plan (TCP-01 through TCP-08) governs staged construction, temporary crossovers, and lane closures.
Utility relocations by others are shown on the Plans; contractor is responsible for coordination and daylighting per the Special Provisions.
The Pecan Creek 100-year peak flow governs demolition and construction sequencing at the bridge; the contractor is responsible for temporary works, dewatering, and coffer measures.
4. CONTRACT FRAMEWORK
Janet Kolb reviewed the contract framework:
Contract Type: Unit-price contract, 118 bid items on the Bid Form.
Engineer's Opinion of Probable Construction Cost Range: $23,000,000 to $26,000,000 (disclosed for planning use only; not a bid restriction).
Retainage: 5% held on earned value, released at Substantial Completion (per General Conditions §7.4).
Liquidated Damages: $2,400 per calendar day beyond the Contract Substantial Completion date (per Contract Article 4).
Prevailing Wages: Federal Wage Decision incorporated as Exhibit C; the City may withhold payment until wage underpayments are corrected and restitution paid (General Conditions §7.8).
Differing Site Conditions: Written notice under General Conditions §4.3 required; the condition must be materially different from those indicated in the Contract Documents.
Stored Materials: Bill of sale and off-site insurance required for payment on stored materials (General Conditions §5.6.2).
Bonds: Performance Bond and Payment Bond, each at 100% of the Contract Amount, issued by a surety acceptable to the City.
5. KEY DATES
The following schedule was reviewed:
Bids shall be submitted in duplicate hard copy in a sealed envelope marked with the Project Name, Project No. WP-2401, and the bidder's name, to the Office of the City Secretary, City of Milbrook, no later than 2:00 p.m. local time on November 12, 2024. Bids received after that time will not be accepted.
6. DBE PARTICIPATION GOAL
Sam DeLuca stated that this project is federally assisted under STP 2024(041) MK and is subject to the City's Disadvantaged Business Enterprise (DBE) Program. The contract-specific DBE participation goal is 8% of the total contract award value.
Each bidder shall submit, with its bid, the DBE Participation Schedule (Form DBE-1) identifying the DBE firms proposed for the work, the scope of work committed to each firm, and the dollar amount of participation. Alternatively, a bidder unable to meet the 8% goal shall submit a Good Faith Efforts documentation package (Form DBE-2) demonstrating adequate good-faith efforts prior to bid opening. Failure to submit either DBE-1 or DBE-2 by the bid deadline will render the bid non-responsive.
DBE directory lookups may be performed through the Texas Unified Certification Program (TUCP) database. Questions regarding DBE eligibility of specific firms shall be directed in writing to the City's DBE Liaison Officer prior to the bid opening.
7. QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS
The following questions were received during the meeting. Where a question is addressed only in these minutes, this record is the sole documentation. Where a question requires a change to the Bid Documents, that change will be issued by formal addendum. Additional written questions will be accepted at jkolb@larkspurcivil.com until 3:00 p.m. on November 7, 2024.
Q-1 (Ironhorse — Petrov): Are the boring logs and geotechnical report by Redoak Geoscience LLC to be relied upon by bidders as the sole indication of subsurface conditions, particularly at Bent 2?
A-1 (Whitfield): The Geotechnical Data Report prepared and sealed by Lisa Fontaine, PE (Redoak Geoscience LLC), including the twelve boring logs B-1 through B-12, is included in the Contract Documents by reference and is available in the bid room and via the procurement portal. Bidders' attention is directed to Section 5.2 of that report, which specifically addresses the pinnacled character of the local limestone and notes that top-of-rock may fluctuate by approximately ±6 ft over lateral offsets on the order of thirty feet due to karst weathering. Boring B-7, located at Bent 2 (Sta. 168+95), records top of rock at elevation 512.3 (NAVD 88). Bidders are advised to review B-7 in conjunction with the §5.2 note in developing their means and methods and pricing for drilled-shaft production.
Q-2 (Vantera — Ballard): What datum controls elevations on the Plans, and how should the existing 1998 utility as-built information (referenced in the Utility Coordination Sheets) be reconciled with the current design?
A-2 (Okafor): All project elevations, structural and roadway, are referenced to NAVD 88. Horizontal control is NAD 83, Texas State Plane Central Zone, U.S. survey feet. The 1998 utility as-built information referenced in the coordination sheets was originally established on NGVD 29 and requires a datum conversion of +0.83 ft to be brought onto the project NAVD 88 basis. This is noted on the survey control memo included in the bid package. Bidders shall not rely on any as-built elevation without applying the noted conversion.
Q-3 (Bluebonnet — Alderman): Sheet C-12 shows storm drain Line B-2 as a 24-inch RCP. Given the tributary area, the bidder's independent capacity check indicates the run is marginal. Please confirm the intended pipe size.
A-3 (Okafor): The Engineer acknowledges the question and confirms that a review of the drainage calculations for Line B-2 is in progress. Addendum No. 1, anticipated for issue on or before November 8, 2024, will reissue Sheet C-12 as C-12R with Line B-2 upsized to 30-inch RCP. Bidders shall bid the addendum-revised size once Addendum No. 1 is issued; acknowledgment of Addendum No. 1 on the Bid Form is mandatory. The Storm-Drainage Design Report (Section 4) will be revised accordingly.
Q-4 (Concho — Escareño): Please confirm the design storm criteria for the storm-drain trunk and for the Pecan Creek crossing.
A-4 (Whitfield): The storm-drain trunk system is designed to a 25-year recurrence-interval design storm using the Rational Method (Q = C · i · A) with IDF data from the Milbrook Drainage Criteria Manual. The Pecan Creek waterway opening, scour analysis, and bridge low-chord clearance are governed by the 100-year recurrence-interval flood, with peak discharge of 4,120 cfs and a 100-year water-surface elevation of 522.4 ft (NAVD 88) at the bridge. The scour analysis follows FHWA HEC-18 / HEC-23.
Q-5 (Summit — Rowe): Please confirm the guardrail system and mounting height at the bridge approaches. Section 606 references a 31-inch MGS. Is the approach rail height governed by that specification, or by a different requirement?
A-5 (DeLuca): Bidders shall bid the guardrail system as shown on the Plans and specified in Technical Specification Section 606 as issued for bid. Any refinement to the approach-rail mounting height, if directed by the City after award to reflect the programmed 3-inch pavement overlay and preserve effective height above the crashworthy minimum, will be handled as a construction-phase directive under the Contract and will not be part of this bidding cycle. Bidders shall not price contingent alternates for guardrail height.
Q-6 (Vantera — Ballard): Please confirm the prevailing wage decision applicable to the project and the certified-payroll reporting cadence.
A-6 (Kolb): The applicable federal wage decision is attached to the Contract as Exhibit C — Federal Wage Decision and is incorporated by reference through General Conditions §7.8. Certified payrolls shall be submitted weekly on Form WH-347 (or equivalent), with signed Statement of Compliance, covering all workers of the Contractor and every subcontractor and lower-tier subcontractor performing work on the project site. Payrolls are due by close of business on the Wednesday following each pay-week ending. Failure to submit compliant certified payrolls, or the presence of uncorrected wage underpayments, may result in withholding of progress payments in accordance with §7.8 until corrections are made and restitution is paid.
Q-7 (Ironhorse — Hines): Are drilled-shaft integrity tests (CSL or thermal) required on the twelve bridge shafts, and if so, how is the testing paid?
A-7 (Whitfield): Cross-hole sonic logging (CSL) is required on every drilled shaft on the project (twelve shafts total). CSL access tubes shall be furnished and installed as specified in Section 416, and the testing is performed by the City's independent testing agency (Pinnacle Testing Services LLC). The installation of access tubes and the Contractor's coordination with the testing agency is subsidiary to the drilled-shaft unit price. Retesting, if triggered by an anomaly, is at the Contractor's expense per the Special Provisions.
Mr. Okafor noted that any additional questions received in writing by 3:00 p.m. on November 7, 2024 will be addressed by formal addendum where a change to the Contract Documents is required, or by written response distributed to all planholders where no change is required.
8. ANTICIPATED ADDENDUM
The Engineer confirmed that Addendum No. 1 will be issued on or before November 8, 2024. Presently anticipated content:
1. Reissue of Sheet C-12 as Sheet C-12R (Rev 1) to upsize storm-drain Line B-2 from 24-inch RCP to 30-inch RCP, with associated revisions to the Storm-Drainage Design Report.
2. Any additional clarifications arising from written questions received by the November 7, 2024 deadline.
Bidders shall acknowledge receipt of Addendum No. 1 on the Bid Form. Failure to acknowledge a duly issued addendum will render the bid non-responsive.
9. GENERAL REMINDERS
Bid security: 5% of the total bid amount, in the form of a bid bond, cashier's check, or certified check payable to the City of Milbrook.
Bid Form must be executed by an authorized officer of the bidder; bidders shall complete the Bidder Qualification Statement and the Non-Collusion Affidavit.
The City reserves the right to reject any or all bids and to waive informalities in accordance with the Instructions to Bidders.
Award will be to the lowest responsive, responsible bidder based on the total bid.
10. ADJOURNMENT
There being no further questions, Mr. Okafor thanked the attendees for their participation. The meeting adjourned at 11:42 a.m.

from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT, WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT
from docx.enum.section import WD_ORIENT
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

NAVY = RGBColor(0x1F, 0x3A, 0x5F)
GRAY = RGBColor(0x59, 0x59, 0x59)
BODY_PT = 10
TABLE_PT = 8.5

doc = Document()

# ---------- page setup ----------
sec = doc.sections[0]
sec.page_width, sec.page_height = Inches(8.5), Inches(11)
sec.left_margin = sec.right_margin = Inches(0.85)
sec.top_margin = Inches(0.7)
sec.bottom_margin = Inches(0.7)
sec.footer_distance = Inches(0.35)

# ---------- base style ----------
st = doc.styles["Normal"]
st.font.name = "Calibri"
st.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn("w:eastAsia"), "Calibri")
st.font.size = Pt(BODY_PT)
st.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
st.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(0)
st.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.07


# ---------- helpers ----------
def shade(cell, hex_fill):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = OxmlElement("w:shd")
    shd.set(qn("w:val"), "clear")
    shd.set(qn("w:color"), "auto")
    shd.set(qn("w:fill"), hex_fill)
    tcPr.append(shd)


def table_borders(table, color="A6A6A6", sz=4, inside=True):
    tbl = table._tbl
    tblPr = tbl.tblPr
    borders = OxmlElement("w:tblBorders")
    edges = ["top", "left", "bottom", "right"] + (["insideH", "insideV"] if inside else [])
    for e in edges:
        el = OxmlElement(f"w:{e}")
        el.set(qn("w:val"), "single")
        el.set(qn("w:sz"), str(sz))
        el.set(qn("w:space"), "0")
        el.set(qn("w:color"), color)
        borders.append(el)
    tblPr.append(borders)


def no_borders(table):
    tbl = table._tbl
    tblPr = tbl.tblPr
    borders = OxmlElement("w:tblBorders")
    for e in ["top", "left", "bottom", "right", "insideH", "insideV"]:
        el = OxmlElement(f"w:{e}")
        el.set(qn("w:val"), "nil")
        borders.append(el)
    tblPr.append(borders)


def cell_margins(table, top=40, bottom=40, left=70, right=70):
    tblPr = table._tbl.tblPr
    mar = OxmlElement("w:tblCellMar")
    for k, v in (("top", top), ("left", left), ("bottom", bottom), ("right", right)):
        el = OxmlElement(f"w:{k}")
        el.set(qn("w:w"), str(v))
        el.set(qn("w:type"), "dxa")
        mar.append(el)
    tblPr.append(mar)


def set_col_widths(table, widths):
    table.autofit = False
    tbl = table._tbl
    tblGrid = tbl.tblGrid
    for i, gc in enumerate(tblGrid.findall(qn("w:gridCol"))):
        gc.set(qn("w:w"), str(int(widths[i].inches * 1440)))
    for row in table.rows:
        for i, cell in enumerate(row.cells):
            cell.width = widths[i]


def repeat_header(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    el = OxmlElement("w:tblHeader")
    el.set(qn("w:val"), "true")
    trPr.append(el)


def no_split(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    el = OxmlElement("w:cantSplit")
    el.set(qn("w:val"), "true")
    trPr.append(el)


def add_runs(p, parts, size=None, color=None):
    """parts: list of (text, style) where style in {'', 'b', 'i', 'bi'}"""
    for text, sty in parts:
        r = p.add_run(text)
        r.bold = "b" in sty
        r.italic = "i" in sty
        if size:
            r.font.size = Pt(size)
        if color is not None:
            r.font.color.rgb = color
    return p


def para(parts, size=None, after=4, before=0, align=None, color=None, keep_next=False, indent=None):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    if isinstance(parts, str):
        parts = [(parts, "")]
    add_runs(p, parts, size=size, color=color)
    pf = p.paragraph_format
    pf.space_after = Pt(after)
    pf.space_before = Pt(before)
    if align is not None:
        p.alignment = align
    if keep_next:
        pf.keep_with_next = True
    if indent is not None:
        pf.left_indent = indent
    return p


def cell_text(cell, parts, size=TABLE_PT, align=None, bold_all=False, color=None, after=0):
    cell.text = ""
    p = cell.paragraphs[0]
    if isinstance(parts, str):
        parts = [(parts, "b" if bold_all else "")]
    add_runs(p, parts, size=size, color=color)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(after)
    p.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.0
    if align is not None:
        p.alignment = align
    cell.vertical_alignment = WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.TOP
    return p

    # bottom rule

    pbdr = OxmlElement("w:pBdr")
    b = OxmlElement("w:bottom")
    b.set(qn("w:val"), "single")
    b.set(qn("w:sz"), "4")
    b.set(qn("w:space"), "1")
    b.set(qn("w:color"), "1F3A5F")
    pbdr.append(b)
    pPr.append(pbdr)

    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    pPr = p._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    pbdr = OxmlElement("w:pBdr")
    b = OxmlElement("w:bottom")
    b.set(qn("w:val"), "single")
    b.set(qn("w:sz"), sz)
    b.set(qn("w:space"), "1")
    b.set(qn("w:color"), color)
    pbdr.append(b)
    pPr.append(pbdr)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(after)
    p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(0)
    r = p.add_run("")
    r.font.size = Pt(2)
    return p

    for i, parts in enumerate(items, 1):
        p = doc.add_paragraph()
        pf = p.paragraph_format
        pf.left_indent = Inches(indent)
        pf.first_line_indent = Inches(-indent)
        pf.space_after = Pt(after)
        tab = pf.tab_stops
        tab.add_tab_stop(Inches(indent))
        add_runs(p, [(f"{i}.\t", "")] + parts, size=size)

    for parts in items:

        pf = p.paragraph_format
        pf.left_indent = Inches(indent)
        pf.first_line_indent = Inches(-indent)
        pf.space_after = Pt(after)
        pf.tab_stops.add_tab_stop(Inches(indent))
        add_runs(p, [("\u2022\t", "")] + parts, size=size)

    fld_begin = OxmlElement("w:fldChar")
    fld_begin.set(qn("w:fldCharType"), "begin")
    instr_el = OxmlElement("w:instrText")
    instr_el.set(qn("xml:space"), "preserve")

r = fp.add_run(" of ")
r.font.size = Pt(7.5)

add_field(r, "NUMPAGES")

Project: | WP-2401 — Wren Parkway Widening & Pecan Creek Bridge Replacement — Federal-Aid STP 2024(041) MK
Subject: | Span 2 deck haunch build-up (SUB-503-04, Calc-C, p. 19) checked against the Contract Documents — not for use as submitted; Contract figures at the profile grade line; steps required before Span 2 deck forms and screed rails are set
-----
1.  BOTTOM LINE
Vantera plans to set the Span 2 deck forms and screed rails the week of May 25 from the haunch build-up in the approved girder package (Lonestar SUB-503-04, Calc-C, p. 19). I checked that build-up against the conformed IFC plans (11/07/2024) and the rest of the Contract Documents. It cannot be used as submitted. Its elevations are not the Contract elevations, it does not follow the B-01 profile, it shows the girders sagging instead of cambering, and it leaves out the slab deflection. The result is a haunch that is too thin at the bearings (2.0/1.9 in. against 3.5 in.), about three times too thick at midspan (6.1 in. against 2.0 in.), and no screed elevations at all.
Effective now, do not set Span 2 deck forms, form-hanger (haunch) adjustments, or screed rails from p. 19 or from the “Elevations at CL bearing (from IFC Sheet B-01)” tables on pp. 7–9. Work that does not fix deck elevations (overhang brackets, staging, edge protection) may continue. The six steps in Section 4 must be completed, in that order, before Span 2 forms are set. Done promptly, they finish by May 28–29 and keep the early-June placement achievable.
Span 2 figures the Contract Documents give at the profile grade line (PGL), NAVD 88. These are check values; basis and limits are in Section 3, and girder-line settings come from Step 4.
Top of girder at the Bent 2 centerline of bearing | 532.98 ft
Haunch at the Bent 2 centerline of bearing | 3.5 in.
Haunch the forms are built to at midspan (bearing haunch taken equal at both bents; design camber of 3.60 in. at forming) | 2.0 in.
Screed-rail elevation at midspan (Sta. 168+42.50) | 534.37 ft
-----
2.  WHY THE SUBMITTED BUILD-UP CANNOT BE USED
Calc-C (p. 19) and the elevation tables it draws on (pp. 7–9) fail on seven counts; Table 1 below sets the numbers side by side.
1.	Its elevations are not from the conformed B-01. Pages 7–9 list “Elevations at CL bearing (from IFC Sheet B-01)” of 536.70, 536.25, 535.73 and 535.28 ft at Abut. 1, Bent 1, Bent 2 and Abut. 2. B-01 gives 534.91, 534.46, 533.93 and 533.48 ft (top of finished concrete deck at the PGL). The package is 1.79–1.80 ft high at every support — a uniform offset that points to some other source, such as a superseded profile. Calc-C does not even match p. 8: its Bent 2 deck soffit (535.47) sits 0.41 ft above p. 8’s own 535.73 less the 8-in. deck.
2.	It does not follow the profile. B-01 carries a constant −0.50% grade across the structure, so the deck soffit falls 0.52 ft between the Span 2 bearings. Calc-C falls 0.12 ft and dips in the middle. The p. 9 note describing a “sag” with a “5.4-in. drop from Abut. 1 to Abut. 2” is wrong on both counts: there is no vertical curve on the bridge, and the drop is 1.43 ft (about 17 in.).
3.	The camber is applied the wrong way. Shop-11 (p. 15) gives the Span 2 girders +3.60 in. of upward camber at erection. Calc-C’s girder-top column puts midspan 5.0 in. below the line between its bearing values — a sag. That is why its haunch grows to 6.1 in. at midspan. On a straight grade, camber makes the midspan haunch thinner than the bearing haunch, not thicker; the p. 19 note that the 6-in. haunch “accommodate[s] the 3.60-in. camber” has it backwards.
4.	The slab deflection is missing and there are no screed elevations. Calc-C sets the finished deck soffit against the girder as it stands before the deck is cast. Forms and screed rails ride on the girders and go down with them under the wet concrete — 2.10 in. at midspan (3.60 in. at erection less 1.50 in. after slab, Shop-11). None of this is in the table.
5.	The bearing haunch is wrong and inconsistent. Calc-C shows 2.0 in. at Bent 1 and 1.9 in. at Bent 2; the Contract Documents give 3.5 in. at Bent 2 (Section 3). The 1.9 in. also misses Calc-C’s own “2.0 in. minimum,” and its note then cites a 1.5-in. minimum and proposes to “adjust haunch shim plate at each bearing.” Re-shimming erected girders changes the B-12 bearing arrangement (see RFI-033 on cumulative build height) and requires the Engineer’s written approval.
6.	It is incomplete. It covers one “sample” line (G2-4) with no cross slope; Span 2 has six lines, 4.25 to 21.25 ft off the PGL, under a 2% crown. It also sends the deck sequence to “Sheet B-06” (p. 21), which is the Abutment 2 sheet; B-11 governs.
7.	The approval does not make it usable. The review was only for conformance with the design concept and the information given (GC §3.4), and the review stamp leaves dimensions with the Contractor. The Engineer’s disposition (p. 24) accepted the strand patterns, losses, camber and end-zone reinforcement — not the Calc-C haunch table or the elevation tables. Shop drawings are not Contract Documents (Agreement Art. 6) and cannot change B-01 (GC §1.4). The package’s own p. 19 note requires measured camber to be verified before deck forms are placed.
Table 1 — Calc-C (sample girder G2-4) compared with the Contract Documents at the PGL (elevations in ft, NAVD 88)
Item | SUB-503-04, p. 19 | Contract Documents (PGL) | Difference
Deck soffit at Bent 1 CL bearing | 535.59 | 533.79 | +1.80 ft
Deck soffit at midspan | 535.46 | 533.53 | +1.93 ft
Deck soffit at Bent 2 CL bearing | 535.47 | 533.27 | +2.20 ft
Fall of deck soffit, Bent 1 to Bent 2 bearing | 0.12 ft, dipping at midspan | 0.52 ft, constant −0.50% grade | profile not followed
Top of girder at Bent 1 / Bent 2 CL bearing | 535.42 / 535.31 | 533.50 / 532.98 | +1.92 / +2.33 ft
Girder top at midspan vs. line between bearings | 5.0 in. below (sag) | 3.60 in. above at erection (Shop-11) | wrong direction
Haunch at Bent 1 / Bent 2 bearings | 2.0 / 1.9 in. | 3.5 / 3.5 in. | 1.5–1.6 in. thin
Haunch at midspan | 6.1 in. | 2.0 in. | 4.1 in. thick
Screed-rail elevations | none given | 534.37 at midspan | missing
-----
G2-4 is 4.25 ft off the PGL; at the 2% crown its deck is about 0.09 ft below the PGL values, which does not change these differences.
If Calc-C were used: forms built to Calc-C’s thicknesses with screed rails at grade would leave the midspan deck about 4 in. thick instead of 8 in. — no room for two mats with the B-10 cover (2½ in. top, 1 in. bottom). Screed rails set off those forms would leave the deck surface about 4 in. high at midspan and 1.5 in. low at the bearings. Calc-C’s elevations used directly would put the deck about 2 ft above B-01.
3.  SPAN 2 FIGURES FROM THE CONTRACT DOCUMENTS (PROFILE GRADE LINE)
Deck forms hang from the girders and the screed rails are carried on them, so both go down with the girders as the deck is placed. The haunch built at forming is therefore the finished haunch, and the screed is set high by the slab deflection. Values are at the PGL, NAVD 88.
Table 2 — Span 2 figures and basis
Figure (PGL) | Value | Basis
Top of girder, Bent 2 CL bearing | 532.98 ft | B-04 top of cap 528.31 (same at both columns) + 2.0-in. net bearing (3.5-in. elastomeric pad seated in a 1.5-in. recess in the girder soffit; B-12 dimensions as carried on approved Shop-12, p. 16) + 54-in. Tx54 modified girder (B-01, B-02, B-07): 528.31 + 0.17 + 4.50 = 532.98.
Haunch, Bent 2 CL bearing | 3.5 in.
(0.29 ft) | Finished deck on the B-01 grade line at the Span 2 bearing (Sta. ≈168+94.75) is 533.94 (B-01 tabulates 533.93 at the bent centerline); less the 8-in. deck (B-01, B-02, B-10) gives a deck soffit of 533.27. 533.27 − 532.98 = 0.29 ft. Using the rounded 533.93 gives 3.4 in.
Haunch the forms are built to, midspan | 2.0 in. | B-01 is a straight −0.50% grade, so there is no vertical-curve ordinate. With the same 3.5-in. haunch at Bent 1 (top of girder 533.50; B-05 in the plan excerpt gives no Bent 1 cap elevation), the deck soffit runs parallel to the girder bearing line, and the only midspan adjustment is the camber left after the slab: 3.60 in. at erection − 2.10 in. slab deflection = 1.50 in. (Shop-11, p. 15 — the camber B-08/B-09 defer to and the EOR disposition accepted). 3.5 − 1.5 = 2.0 in. At forming: girder top 533.54 (bearing line 533.24 + 3.60 in.); form soffit 533.71 (finished soffit 533.53 + 2.10 in.).
Screed-rail elevation, midspan | 534.37 ft | B-01 finished deck at Sta. 168+42.50 (midway between both the bent and the bearing centerlines): 534.46 − 0.005 × 52.5 = 534.1975 (534.20); plus the 2.10-in. (0.175-ft) slab dead-load deflection the screed must anticipate (Shop-11): 534.1975 + 0.175 = 534.37.
-----
Notes on these figures
•	Check values, not setting values. They are at the PGL with the design camber. No girder sits on the PGL: the lines are 4.25, 12.75 and 21.25 ft off it, where the 2% crown (C-02; B-02 for gutter-line elevations) puts the deck soffit about 1.0, 3.1 and 5.1 in. lower.
•	Measured camber governs the midspan haunch. For a measured midspan camber C (in.) at forming, midspan haunch = 3.5 − (C − 2.10): under 2.0 in. once C passes 3.60 in., under 1.5 in. past 4.10 in., and zero at 5.60 in. Shop-11’s ±25% erection tolerance (2.70–4.50 in.) spans 2.9 down to 1.1 in. of haunch. Yard-01 scheduled the Span 2 casts for 03/09/2026 (G2-1 to G2-3) and 03/23/2026 (G2-4 to G2-6); at an early-June pour those girders would be about 70 to 88 days old, past Shop-11’s 60-day basis, and the two groups will not camber alike. The record has no Span 2 erection camber readings (Update 15 shows Span 2 erected 04/09/2026, which DR-0324 contradicts — the Bent 2 cap was placed 04/30/2026).
•	Seats must step for the crown. B-04 lists one top-of-cap elevation (528.31) at both columns. With the 2% crown the exterior-line deck soffit is about 5 in. below the PGL, so seat or pad height has to step by girder line per the B-12 schedule; a level seat under all six lines would put the exterior girders about 1.6 in. above the deck soffit at the bearings. The record has no as-built seat survey for Bent 2.
•	Screed basis. The screed figure carries slab dead-load deflection only (Shop-11 “after slab”), with the slab acting on simple-span girders — true under the B-11 sequence (continuity forms when the closure concrete cures) and under the RFI-047 proposal. The later change to the +0.85-in. long-term camber is not built in unless the EOR directs. If the RFI-047 response changes the deflection basis, the screed must be re-issued with it; B-11 General Note 3 bars any other sequence without a sealed analysis approved before placement.
•	Other. B-01 elevations are top of finished concrete deck; the programmed 3-in. overlay (bid item 458; B-14) sits above them. Spec 502.01 still cites “AASHTO BT-72 or equivalent” on “Sheets S-5 through S-9”; the conformed girder sheets (B-07 to B-09) and the girders as fabricated are Tx54 modified, 54 in. deep.

steps.message:
I've drafted the memo for Dana's signature and saved it as `/filesystem/Span2_Haunch_Verification.docx` (4 pages, dated May 21, 2026). The answer is **no**: the Span 2 build-up in the approved girder package can't be used as submitted.

**Why it fails against the contract documents**
- **Wrong elevations.** The elevations the package says come from Sheet B-01 are 1.79–1.80 ft higher than B-01 at every support.
- **Wrong profile.** B-01 is a straight −0.5% grade, so the deck should drop 0.52 ft across Span 2. The package's table drops 0.12 ft and dips in the middle.
- **Camber backwards.** The table shows the girders sagging 5.0 in. at midspan, but the package's own camber diagram has them cambering 3.60 in. upward. That's why its haunch grows to 6.1 in. at midspan instead of shrinking.
- **No slab deflection and no screed elevations.** The 2.10 in. the girders drop under the wet deck isn't accounted for anywhere.
- **Bearing haunch wrong.** The table shows 2.0 and 1.9 in.; the contract documents give 3.5 in. The 1.9 in. is also below the package's own 2.0-in. minimum.
- **The approval doesn't cover it.** Larkspur's approval was limited to strand patterns, losses, camber and end-zone reinforcement, not the haunch table. Shop drawings aren't contract documents and can't override B-01.

**Span 2 figures from the contract documents at the profile grade line**

| Figure | Value | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Top of girder, Bent 2 centerline of bearing | 532.98 ft | B-04 cap 528.31 + 2.0 in. net bearing + 54-in. girder |
| Haunch at that bearing | 3.5 in. | B-01 deck 533.94 − 8-in. deck − 532.98 |
| Haunch the forms are built to at midspan | 2.0 in. | 3.5 in. − 1.50 in. of camber left after the slab |
| Screed-rail elevation at midspan (Sta. 168+42.50) | 534.37 ft | B-01 deck 534.20 + 2.10 in. slab deflection |

The memo says these are check values only. Girder-line settings have to come from a survey of the actual girder tops, because camber at the real girder ages will differ from the design value.

**Order of steps before the forms go on**
1. Stop using the table now and mark the copies void.
2. Vantera surveys the actual girder tops and bearing seats on all six Span 2 lines, with Larkspur check shots.
3. In parallel, Priya confirms the design inputs, including the bearing pad schedule on Sheet B-12 and the slab deflection values.
4. Vantera and Lonestar submit a revised, sealed haunch and screed sheet.
5. Larkspur reviews and issues a disposition.
6. Vantera sets the forms, and Larkspur verifies them before rebar goes in.

The target dates run May 21–29, which keeps the early-June pour possible. Monday, May 25 is Memorial Day.

**Decisions for you**
- **Addressee:** I addressed the memo to Vantera (Ballard and Tate), copying Priya, Marcus, Tom, Lonestar and the City Engineer, so it also serves as the stop notice. If Dana would rather keep it internal, only the To line needs changing.
- **Bearing recess:** The 2.0-in. net bearing depends on the 3.5-in. pad sitting in a 1.5-in. recess in the girder. That comes from the girder package, which cites Sheet B-12, but B-12's bearing schedule isn't in the plan set on the share. If there were no recess, the bearing haunch would be 2.0 in. and the midspan haunch only 0.5 in. That's why Priya's B-12 confirmation is step 3.
- **Camber values:** The camber and slab deflection figures come from the girder package's camber diagram, which the girder sheets (B-08/B-09) defer to.
- **Bent 1:** As you asked, the Bent 1 haunch is taken as equal to Bent 2's.

The memo also flags some inconsistencies I found in the project record:
- **Erection date:** Schedule Update 15 shows the Span 2 girders erected April 9, but the April 30 daily report records the Bent 2 cap only just poured.
- **Submittal log:** The log dates the girder package approval to July 2025, but the package on file is stamped February 18, 2026.
